newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Prices propped up by tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Prices propped up by tight supplies.

text.p: Asia's crude market was supported on Wednesday due to tighter supplies of light grades and limited West African availabilities for September, traders said.
September is traditionally a strong buying period for light grades.
But the limited supplies of light Australian crudes were expected to push buyers to buy the heavier crudes as alternatives, providing support to these grades.
Prices of late-August heavy sweet Minas and Widuri crudes had taken a beating, after trading at strong premiums in July and early August.
Minas was discussed around ICP +30 cents per barrel over the last fortnight, compared to July trades at ICP +75 cents.
But sellers of September cargoes of Minas and Widuri were now holding out for higher prices.
The Middle East crude market was also steady, despite the imminent arrival of Iraqi crude.
But September trading for Middle East grades were also completed, with only Masila and few cargoes of Abu Dhabi grades on offer.
"The fact that most Middle East cargoes are already committed shows that the market is quite balanced without Iraqi crude," a western trader said.
"With Iraqi crude, the market will be slightly oversupplied, but won't be flooded," he said.
Some traders said Iraqi crude exports will have a bearish impact on the Asian crude market, but in a less direct way.
A greater volume of Iraqi crude was expected to head west, which will pull down the benchmark grades Brent and WTI, they said.
"Brent prices will come down, which will make West African crudes relatively cheaper compared to Asian grades, opening the arbitrage window to Asia," a trader said.
September Masila was heard sold to a US major at Dubai +25 cents, a fair reflection of the current market, traders said.
